book.title: The Telegraph All New Toughie Crossword, book 1

clue.text: Mostly worked as fisherman, taking in quite peculiar behaviour of surfers?

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of it, so the final letter of the word is dropped
something peculiar is odd or out of shape, so these letters are put into a strange new order
to take something in is to hold it inside, so one piece goes into the middle of another

blocks.note: a fisherman who works with a net has netted his catch
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An angler who spends spare time studying the odd ways of wave-riders.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters sit inside the shortened fishing word, after its third letter. The surfers are web surfers, not beach ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Netiquette is the code of polite conduct expected of people using the internet, who are said to surf the web.

clue.text: Brass bottle's top

blocks.note: first meaning: cheek or nerve
second meaning: the narrow upper part of a bottle

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a brass bottle, but brass is slang for impudence.
explanation.definitionFit: Neck is British slang for impudence, like brass, and also names the narrow upper part of a bottle.

clue.text: Vehicle, expensive vehicle, not quite fitting in the yard

indicators.note: not quite means falling just short, so the final letter is dropped
fitting in places one piece snugly inside the other

blocks.note: the opening letters of these two words
a Roller is slang for a Rolls-Royce

explanation.surface: A pricey car that will not quite fit into the yard.
explanation.walkthrough: ROLLER minus its last letter goes between T and Y. Nothing in the clue signals taking the first letters of 'the yard', so that part of the parse is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A trolley is a small wheeled cart, and in some places a name for a tram, so it is a vehicle.

clue.text: Senior lawyer in New York area letting slip no clues

indicators.note: letting things slip lets them fall out of place, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: Queens is one of New York City's five boroughs
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A top New York attorney gives nothing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letting slip no clues' looks like discretion, but the two words are the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen's Counsel is the title of a senior barrister in Britain, appointed on merit.

clue.text: Unoccupied? Look to replace time in occupation

indicators.note: to replace says one piece takes the place of another inside the word

blocks.note: a place unoccupied is empty
lo! is an old word meaning look
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone without a job is told to find a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unoccupied?' looks like the definition at the start, but it is the word worked on; the definition is the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Employ means employment or a job, as in 'in the employ of', so it is a person's occupation.

clue.text: Skilful chess champion participated, losing Queen

indicators.note: losing something means going without it, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: Mikhail Tal was world chess champion in 1960
someone who participated entered the contest
R, for Regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A gifted chess master played on even after giving up his queen.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess setting makes Queen look like the piece, but it stands for R, removed from ENTERED.
explanation.definitionFit: Talented means having natural ability, which is what skilful describes.

clue.text: Theoretical physicist's a dull lecturer to hear

indicators.note: to hear points to what the words sound like when spoken, not how they are written

blocks.note: a tedious speaker is a bore

explanation.surface: A jibe that some great scientist was tedious in the lecture hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Niels Bohr was the Danish physicist whose theory of the atom underpins quantum mechanics.

clue.text: Drugs work? Is getting worried at heart

indicators.note: at heart means in the very middle, so that piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: op is short for opus, a work
taken as written
worried as in 'what's eating you?', so ate

explanation.surface: Do these medicines really work? An anxious patient asks.
explanation.walkthrough: Worried here means troubled, as in 'what's eating you?', so its past tense is the eating word.
explanation.definitionFit: Opiates are drugs derived from opium, such as morphine.

clue.text: Unusual boat and sailor left in stormy mere

indicators.note: a stormy sea is churned up, so the letters are thrown into a new order
in puts the vessel, sailor and left inside the rearranged word

blocks.note: Noah's ark is the famous boat
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An odd vessel with a sailor stranded on a rough lake.
explanation.walkthrough: A mere is a lake, an old and poetic word still used in English place names.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable means worthy of notice because out of the ordinary, which is what unusual describes.

clue.text: Fail to win in trophy? That's the big picture

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other, here the failure inside the prize

blocks.note: a cup is a common sporting trophy
to lose is to fail to win

explanation.surface: A sports pundit shrugging off a lost final as part of the wider view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The big picture' looks like the overall view, but it means a shot in which the subject fills the frame and looks big.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-up is a camera shot taken near the subject, so it shows that subject large on screen.

clue.text: Reactive metal ignited gas, forcing the Spanish to flee

indicators.note: making something flee drives it out, so those letters leave the word for the gas

blocks.note: something ignited has been lit
helium is a light, unreactive gas
el is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A lab accident: a metal sparks, gas catches fire, and the Spanish visitors run for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures Spaniards fleeing a fire; really the Spanish article simply leaves the gas's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithium is an alkali metal that reacts readily with water and air, so it is kept under oil.

clue.text: Agree mirth out of place when encountering a death?

indicators.note: letters out of place have to be put back in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
a as in 'ten pounds a head', meaning per

explanation.surface: Laughter is out of place when someone has just died.
explanation.walkthrough: The small word 'a' is easy to read past; it supplies PER for the mix. The question mark marks the definition as a personification.
explanation.definitionFit: The Grim Reaper is the hooded figure with a scythe who personifies death.

clue.text: Playing in concert, Nell ... finds herself here?

definitions.text: Playing in concert, Nell ... finds herself here?

indicators.note: playing suggests the words are being performed freely, so their letters are moved about

blocks.note: every letter of these three words is used

explanation.surface: A performer called Nell, booked for a concert, ends up at a famous venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition. The American spelling CENTER is needed; the crossings confirm the final ER.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lincoln Center is New York's performing arts complex, home to concert halls, so a musician playing there would find herself in it.

clue.text: I work on soul with art, possibly praising pagan gods

indicators.note: possibly hints the words are one arrangement of several, so their letters are shuffled

blocks.note: taken as written
to do is to work
taken as written, then rearranged
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: An artist pours their spirit into work that celebrates heathen deities.
explanation.walkthrough: I and DO come first, then SOUL and ART rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Idolatrous means given to worshipping idols, the images of false or pagan gods.

clue.text: Gamble about railway — it merely looks like steam

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: to dice is to gamble, as with dice
RY is the standard abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A wager on the railway, and the cloud around an engine turns out to be fake steam.
explanation.walkthrough: The railway and steam point to steam trains, but the vapour here is a stage effect.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry ice is frozen carbon dioxide, which gives off a white fog used on stage to imitate mist or steam.

clue.text: Failed banker swallowing arsenic, in a state

indicators.note: something that has failed has collapsed, so its letters are reassembled differently
swallowing takes something inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
As is the chemical symbol for arsenic

explanation.surface: A ruined banker takes poison and is found in a bad way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a state' reads as 'very upset', but 'a state' is the definition and 'in' only joins it on.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebraska is one of the fifty states of the USA, in the Great Plains.

clue.text: Water creature — make mistake, putting it in sink?

indicators.note: putting it in places the first piece inside the second

blocks.note: in golf, to sink a short putt is to tap it in
to err is to make a mistake

explanation.surface: Fumbling an aquatic animal into the kitchen sink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting' and 'sink' look domestic, but they are golf: a tap-in sinks the ball, and ERR goes inside it after T.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a small freshwater turtle, an animal that lives in water.

clue.text: Genuine backing about our following British working man

indicators.note: backing means going backwards, so the word is read from end to start
following says one piece comes straight after the other
about means surrounding, so the other pieces go inside

blocks.note: genuine means real
B is the abbreviation for British
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sincere support from us for the ordinary British worker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' looks like support for the worker, but it turns the word for genuine round.
explanation.definitionFit: A labourer does manual work for wages, the classic image of the working man.

clue.text: Word for drink supplier unknown to lexicographer

definitions.note: the clue frames the definition as 'a word for drink supplier'

blocks.note: E. Cobham Brewer compiled Brewer's Dictionary of Phrase and Fable
y is one of the algebraic unknowns

explanation.surface: A dictionary compiler has never come across the word for a drinks maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unknown to lexicographer' looks like a word missing from a dictionary, but it is the unknown Y added to the lexicographer.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewery is the business that makes and supplies beer, so it supplies drink.

clue.text: A person dismissing half of it as 'not ethical'

indicators.note: half of a two-letter word is a single letter, here the back half
dismissing sends something away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: A taken as written, and a person is a mortal
the second half of this two-letter word

explanation.surface: Someone sniffily dismissing something as unethical.
explanation.walkthrough: A MORTAL loses its T to leave AMORAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoral describes someone or something without moral principles, outside ethics altogether.

clue.text: Wine container, top off, overturned

indicators.note: with its top off, a down word loses its first letter
something overturned is upside down, so in a down entry the letters run the other way

blocks.note: a canister is a container

explanation.surface: A bottle or cask of wine knocked over with its lid off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wine container' reads as one thing, a carafe or cask, but Wine alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Roman general snaps up one heading for Ostia

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top
a heading is the top, so just the first letter is taken

blocks.note: snaps are photos, or pics
the Roman numeral for one
the first letter of this word

explanation.surface: A Roman commander seizes someone on the road to Ostia, the port of ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snaps up' looks like seizing, but snaps are photos and up turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: Scipio Africanus was the Roman general who defeated Hannibal at Zama in 202 BC.

clue.text: Source of wealth certainly within reach in cricket match

indicators.note: within puts the word for certainty inside the word for reach
in puts that combination inside the word for the match

blocks.note: a Test is an international cricket match
taken as written
sure! means certainly

explanation.surface: A batsman's fortune seems close at hand during a big game.
explanation.walkthrough: Two nested containers: the innermost goes inside reach, and that whole goes inside the match after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasure chest is a box full of valuables, and figuratively any rich supply of good things.

clue.text: Fail to apply, missing one burst of activity

indicators.note: missing means going without, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: to waive a rule is to decline to apply it
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Neglecting to put in an application, then a sudden flurry of effort.
explanation.definitionFit: A wave is a sudden surge of something, as in a crime wave or a wave of strikes.

clue.text: Cricket and athletics events to occupy same period?

blocks.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket
a lap is one circuit of the track in athletics

explanation.surface: A sports scheduler worrying that a cricket match and an athletics meeting clash.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark covers 'occupy same period', which defines the word as two things sharing time.
explanation.definitionFit: Two events overlap when part of one happens during part of the other.

clue.text: Seasoning soft food recipe? One starts in kitchen area

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters only

blocks.note: pap is soft mushy food for babies or invalids
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin recipe, 'take'
the Roman numeral for one
the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A cook wondering about a recipe for a bland dish, set in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: Paprika is a red powdered spice made from dried sweet peppers, used to season food.

clue.text: Prince's destination - the blue yonder, with second of helicopters

indicators.note: second of picks out the letter in position two of the next word

blocks.note: the wild blue yonder is the sky
the second letter of this word

explanation.surface: A royal flies off into the distance by helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonnie Prince Charlie escaped 'over the sea to Skye' in 1746, as the Skye Boat Song tells.
explanation.definitionFit: Skye is the Hebridean island where Bonnie Prince Charlie fled after his defeat at Culloden.

clue.text: Aggressive positioning of the eyes?

blocks.note: first meaning: blatantly confrontational
second meaning, taken literally: where your eyes sit

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second meaning as a literal reading of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes bold, confrontational behaviour, and read literally it is where a person's eyes are placed.
